wikidata.note: checked: coordinates and description on Wikidata match the lake at Les Gaillands, 45.914 N 6.848 E, 'lake in France'

draw.note: No designation; the tourism board lists it as a climbing site with a lake and picnic area, 2 km from Chamonix.

standing.note: A pleasant valley-floor lake with a Mont Blanc reflection; the alpine lakes are the stronger version.

distinction.note: Lac de l'Anglais beside it, Lac des Chavants (Les Houches), Lac Vert and the alpine lakes of the Aiguilles Rouges, all within 25 km.

easy_payoff.note: Roadside: the lake and the reflection are next to the car park.

weather.note: The reflection of the massif needs clear, still air; a lakeside picnic still works in cloud.

records.why: A flat lakeside picnic with Mont Blanc reflected, 2 km from town.

designations.note: No own or parent designation found on the page read.

wikidata.note: checked: coordinates and description on Wikidata match the aerial tramway, 45.918 N 6.870 E; the mountain is Q404728

draw.note: The tourism board's headline lift: one rise from 1,033 m to 3,842 m; timed tickets, new ones released the day before, sell out on clear mornings.

standing.note: The highest and best-known lift in the Mont Blanc valleys.

distinction.note: The Skyway Monte Bianco from Courmayeur (Pointe Helbronner, 3,466 m) is the one comparable lift within 100 km.

records.unique_because: One continuous cable-car rise of about 2,800 m to 3,842 m.

easy_payoff.note: The cable car is the easy way; the view is at the terraces.

weather.note: In cloud the summit shows nothing and the lift may stop.

records.why: A single cable car rise to 3,842 m, face to face with Mont Blanc.

v.note: timed slots; new tickets released the day before (D-1); pass holders must reserve too

designations.note: The Mont Blanc massif holds no UNESCO or park designation; none found on the page read.

wikidata.note: checked: coordinates and description on Wikidata match the Montenvers rack railway, 'railway line in France'; the viewpoint is Q1946088

draw.note: The tourism board's classic Mer de Glace outing; the glacier is France's largest (Wikidata Q583591).

standing.note: The only lift to the Mer de Glace viewpoint.

distinction.note: The Aiguille du Midi and Brevent lifts give other high views, but not of a valley glacier this close.

easy_payoff.note: The train is the easy way to the viewpoint.

weather.note: The viewpoint wants clear air; the ice cave and the Glaciorium work in cloud.

records.why: A rack railway to the Mer de Glace, with the glacier's retreat marked on the stairs.

designations.note: No designation found on the page read.

wikidata.note: checked: coordinates and description on Wikidata match Emosson Dam, Finhaut, Valais, 46.068 N 6.932 E

draw.note: A free dam viewpoint listed by the Chamonix and Valais tourism boards; the footprints need a difficult 4 h 40 hike.

standing.note: A strong half-day across the Swiss border; the footprints are the unusual part.

distinction.note: Few dinosaur trackways are open to walkers in the Alps; big dams with Mont Blanc views are less rare.

easy_payoff.note: The dam top and its Mont Blanc view are easy; the footprints need the 12.9 km, +845 m hike.

weather.note: The Mont Blanc view needs clear air; the footprints are snow-free only from about mid-July.

records.why: A high dam with a view to Mont Blanc and 240-million-year-old footprints above it.

access_cost.note: Post bus or funicular; neither is a booking. The funicular's status conflicts between sources.

designations.note: No designation found on the pages read.

wikidata.note: checked: coordinates and description on Wikidata match 'Ice cave in France', 45.927 N 6.922 E

draw.note: Part of the tourism board's Montenvers visit; re-cut in the glacier each year.

standing.note: The best-known glacier ice cave in the area; about 200 stairs each way.

distinction.note: Glacier ice grottoes elsewhere in the Alps lie beyond 100 km.

easy_payoff.note: The gondola and stairs are the only way; no harder version exists.

weather.note: Inside the glacier; works in any weather.

records.why: A walk-through cave cut into the Mer de Glace, re-carved every year.

designations.note: No designation found on the page read.

draw.note: Host of the first Winter Olympics (1924) and the tourism board's base for the whole massif; the one town the region is known by.

standing.note: The main town of the valley.

distinction.note: Courmayeur (15 km through the tunnel) and Zermatt (beyond 100 km) are the comparable resort towns.

weather.note: Shops, museum and cafes work in rain.

records.why: The mountaineering capital, with Mont Blanc over its main street.

draw.note: A weekly town market; the tourism board lists it as a practical service, not a headline.

standing.note: A good Saturday market; Annecy's markets are larger.

weather.note: Outdoors; it runs in light rain.

records.why: A Saturday morning market on Place du Mont-Blanc.

standing.note: A quiet base beside a lift and the train line.

distinction.note: Other hamlets on the line: Les Bois, Les Tines, Argentiere.

weather.note: A village stroll works in any weather.

wikidata.note: checked: coordinates and description on Wikidata match the Aiguillette des Posettes summit, 46.018 N 6.940 E; the trip stop 'Col des Montets' is the start area, Q948024

draw.note: A tourism board route sheet, rated Moyenne; no designation of its own.

standing.note: A strong balcony view of the Mont Blanc massif and the Glacier du Tour; Brevent and Lac Blanc are more famous.

distinction.note: The Aiguilles Rouges balconies (Brevent, Flegere, Lac Blanc, Cheserys) within 15 km.

easy_payoff.note: The Vallorcine gondola to the Col des Posettes, when it runs, cuts most of the climb.

weather.note: The ridge view needs clear air.

records.why: A ridge walk with Mont Blanc and the Glacier du Tour in one view.

access_cost.note: No booking; the gondola shortcut is optional.

designations.note: No designation found on the route sheet.

wikidata.note: checked: coordinates and description on Wikidata match Lac Blanc in the Aiguilles Rouges, 45.982 N 6.889 E (not the Vosges Lac Blanc, Q267332); the trail has no item

draw.note: Inside the Aiguilles Rouges nature reserve (parent); the tourism board's best-known lake hike, with the massif reflected.

standing.note: The valley's most famous lake walk.

distinction.note: The Cheserys lakes (1 km) and Lac Cornu share the view; nothing else in the region matches the full reflection.

easy_payoff.note: The Index chairlift route (2.9 km) is shorter, but still a mountain path.

weather.note: The reflection needs a clear, calm day.

records.why: The Mont Blanc massif mirrored in a lake at 2,352 m.

v.note: via the Flegere gondola; the walk from Les Praz adds about 800 m

designations.quote: the path is in the Nature Reserve Les Aiguilles Rouges

weather.note: Views of the needles want clear air.
